# Synthetic PDF fixtures

Test inputs for knowledge-document text extraction (ADR-0026). Every file is synthetic: no real
clinic or patient data. They are generated by `scripts/generate-test-pdfs.py` (development only;
it needs Python with reportlab, DejaVu Sans, qpdf and LibreOffice). CI uses these committed files
and never runs the generator.

| File                            | What it exercises                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `english.pdf`                   | Paragraphs, a line break inside a paragraph, a page boundary       |
| `greek.pdf`                     | Greek text                                                         |
| `arabic-presentation-forms.pdf` | Arabic presentation forms in visual order (NFKC)                   |
| `libreoffice-arabic-greek.pdf`  | A real word processor's Arabic and Greek (known Arabic limitation) |
| `ligatures.pdf`                 | Latin ligatures                                                    |
| `standard-font.pdf`             | A standard (non-embedded) font, with no font data configured       |
| `embedded-link.pdf`             | A link annotation: no network access                               |
| `many-paragraphs.pdf`           | Multi-page chunking                                                |
| `pages-100.pdf`                 | Exactly the page limit                                             |
| `pages-101.pdf`                 | One page over the limit                                            |
| `high-text-ratio.pdf`           | A small file with text far over the character limit                |
| `scanned.pdf`                   | An image-only page (no text layer)                                 |
| `empty.pdf`                     | A blank page                                                       |
| `encrypted-password.pdf`        | Needs a password to open                                           |
| `encrypted-owner-only.pdf`      | Encrypted, but opens without a password                            |
| `truncated.pdf`                 | A valid signature followed by a broken structure                   |
